stages.a: The bag top is cut off, leaving a plastic collar above the block. Water beads inside it.
stages.v: One common opening: cut the top off after pins form, leaving a collar. Condensation runs down the collar into the pins and floods them.

stages.a: Pins rise from the top centre of the block.
stages.v: Fruit from the top centre; side growth is unwanted. Strongly light-triggered: bright, deep, even light.

stages.a: Thick white stems swell and stretch upward with small caps on top.
stages.v: Run the exhaust in cycles from a CO2 controller. Bleached, crusty, flat beige caps mean too much CO2 and too little light.

stages.a: Fat stems; the caps are open and rounded.
stages.v: Even, intense light gives uniform round caps; uneven light gives fluted, sideways caps. Kings keep very well.

stages.a: The caps flatten and their edges turn up.
stages.v: Fruit cold (10-16 °C). Above 16 °C expect blotch and humidity trouble.

labels.a: The plastic collar left when the bag top is cut off.
labels.v: The collar is the hardest method, though many think it the safest.

labels.a: Water beading on the inside of the collar.
labels.v: Warm substrate meets cooler incoming air and the water runs down into the pins. Small slits before opening help.

labels.a: Pins rising from the top centre.
labels.v: Fruit from the top centre; side growth is unwanted.

labels.a: The fat white stem: the part people buy.
A small cap on top of the stem.
labels.v: Bleached, crusty, flat beige caps mean too much CO2 and too little light.
Even, intense light gives uniform round caps.

labels.a: Gills run down the top of the stem.
The cap flattens and its edge turns up.
